I've reviewed the CSV and the sample remittance. Preliminary notes:

1) VAT withholding appears on 12 merchant accounts (rows 24-35 in the CSV) with a "VAT w/hold" qualifier. Those are bank-level withholdings (UK intermediary) rather than merchant invoiced VAT. We have two paths:
   - Recognize a "VAT recoverable" receivable (asset) and keep the original revenue intact, then reverse when we receive reimbursement from the bank or merchant.
   - If we expect non-recovery > 90 days, take a provisional reduction to revenue and book an allowance.

2) Several settlement IDs had truncated invoice references after the cutover; payments ops did not carry legacy invoice tokens into the new manifest — causing unapplied cash.

Suggested accounting actions (draft attached as journal_draft_IZ-907.pdf):
- JE 1 (temporary): Debit Bank Suspense (1150) £54,832 / Credit Settlements Clearing (2100) £54,832 — to reflect received cash that cannot be matched to invoices yet.
- JE 2 (VAT recoverable): Debit VAT Recoverable (1340) £9,766 / Credit VAT Withholding Contra (4900) £9,766 — for the 20% withholding portion across the flagged merchants.
- JE 3 (reclassification when matched): Move amounts from Bank Suspense -> AR with invoice references once payments ops provides mapping.

Action owners: Marcus to prepare JE and accounting memo; Kimberly to provide matching file and advise on bank recovery likelihood; Priyom/Laura to handle external comms with ACME/merchant contacts.

I've attached a draft journal and a short memo with GL account suggestions. If we need sign-off for an allowance, finance will route to FP&A.

Attachments: journal_draft_IZ-907.pdf

–Marcus
Manager, Revenue Operations

Quick update after payments ops review and bank repro: we can map ~70% of the shortfalls back to invoices using bank trace IDs. The remaining ~30% corresponds to two merchant bank partners that withheld VAT at source and marked remits as "statutory hold." PayStream confirms they issued withholding certificates for the larger accounts — attaching the cert we received from Acme (vat_withholding_cert_acme.pdf).

For the mapped items: we will apply unapplied cash to the matching invoices today and send a remittance confirmation to ACME. For the VAT-withheld items: payments ops recommends we book VAT Recoverable as Marcus suggested; then create a follow-up task to send the VAT certificate to Treasury for recovery. If recovery fails in 90 days, move to allowance.

I've also attached bank_remit_20260831.pdf extracts where you can see the "VAT w/hold" line. I've copied the column-level mapping to the Drive link in the related_links field.

Next steps (summary):
- Marcus: finalize JEs and post temporary suspense entries by EOD.
- Kimberly: apply mapped cash, produce a remittance file for ACME, and escalate the two withholding merchants for Treasury follow-up.
- Priyom: confirm external comms and whether ACME expects Redwood to pursue the recovery or if they will (impacts commercial credit).

Thanks — Kim
